clue.text: Keep quiet about woman who appreciates Greek culture?

definitions.note: a clause standing for a person, 'one who appreciates Greek culture'

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, so the hush word wraps the woman's name

parts.note: hist is an old interjection calling for quiet, like 'hush!'
Ellen is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone told to hush about a woman with a taste for Greek culture.
explanation.walkthrough: HIST is a dated call for silence; put it about ELLEN to get H-ELLEN-IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar or admirer of ancient Greek language and civilisation is known by this name.

clue.text: The man will act violently — as will she

parts.note: the man will contracts to he'll

indicators.note: acting violently throws the letters of act about into a new order

explanation.surface: A man promises to behave violently, and a woman says she will too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' is the anagram signal on 'act'. The definition 'she' is fair because the answer is a fierce, spiteful woman, and the surface makes her as violent as the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiteful, violent-tempered woman is called this, so it names a particular kind of she.

clue.text: Don't keep up young lady who's been upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for the young lady upside down, reading it from the bottom

parts.note: gal is informal for a girl or young lady

explanation.surface: Advice not to keep pace with a girl who has been distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns GAL to read upwards, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail behind and fail to keep pace is a plain verb synonym of falling behind.

clue.text: Attractive county opener getting out topping!

indicators.note: the opener, the first letter, getting out means the county loses its initial; also a cricket pun on a batsman dismissed

parts.note: Kent is an English county in the south-east
icing is the sweet topping on a cake

explanation.surface: A county cricket opening batsman being dismissed is wonderful news.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county. 'opener getting out' reads as cricket, a county side's opening batsman dismissed, but signals losing a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alluring or tempting draws people in, which is what attractive means here.

clue.text: Like some architecture sending a tongue-in-cheek message — not right

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a tongue-in-cheek message is ironic

explanation.surface: A building style that seems to wink at the viewer, minus a correct touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from IRONIC.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the classical orders of Greek columns, with scroll capitals, describes such buildings.

clue.text: Outwardly secure, a bad fitting on back of bike?

indicators.note: outwardly says the word for secure stands outside, wrapping the other pieces

parts.note: tight means fixed or secure
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A badly fitted part on the rear of a bicycle, held fast from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' looks like it describes the bike part, but it tells you the secure word goes round the others; 'a bad fitting' reads as a poorly fitted part.
explanation.definitionFit: The red lamp mounted at the rear of a bicycle or vehicle is exactly such a fitting.

clue.text: What when flailed could make one sweat?

definitions.text: What when flailed could make one sweat?

indicators.note: flailed means thrashed about wildly, so the letters of sweat are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A riddle about an implement that would make someone sweat when swung.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of SWEAT, flailed, give the answer, which is itself a Scottish leather strap once used to punish schoolchildren, so being thrashed with it would make one sweat.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather strap with tongues, formerly used in Scottish schools for corporal punishment.

clue.text: Odin's son has a mark on map to denote treasure chest

parts.note: in Norse myth Thor is the son of Odin

parts.words: mark on map to denote treasure
parts.note: X marks the spot of buried treasure on a pirate map

explanation.surface: A Norse god marks a treasure chest's location with a cross on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treasure chest' looks like one item, but 'treasure' ends the wordplay and 'chest' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomically, the part of the body between neck and abdomen is the chest.

clue.text: Report of road game that may give car a sort of assessment

definitions.text: that may give car a sort of assessment

indicators.note: report of means said aloud, the phrase is heard as another

parts.note: way is a road and bridge is a card game, together way-bridge

explanation.surface: Talk of a game on the road leading to a car being inspected.
explanation.walkthrough: WAY (road) plus BRIDGE (the card game) is said aloud as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform scale for weighing vehicles assesses a car's weight, hence a sort of assessment.

clue.text: Not stopping outside when sign of affection has been denied

indicators.note: denied means the kiss is refused, so that letter is removed

parts.note: external means outside
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going outdoors after being refused a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been denied' takes X out of EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Everlasting, without end, is the same as never stopping.

clue.text: Get blonde in boat shortly before noon

indicators.note: before places the trimmed boat ahead of the letter for noon
shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for loading ships

explanation.surface: Someone bleaching their hair on a boat just before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: A lighter is a flat barge used to ferry cargo to ships, a meaning many solvers miss; 'shortly' trims its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair that becomes paler goes blonde, as a verb meaning to make or become lighter in colour.

clue.text: Pay inordinate attention to frivolous viewers wanting a hearing

indicators.note: a hearing means being listened to, so the phrase is heard aloud as another word

parts.note: idle eyes: idle means frivolous and eyes are viewers

explanation.surface: Fans fixated on stars, their idle eyes wanting to be listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: IDLE EYES, spoken, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or revere someone excessively is to give them inordinate attention.

clue.text: This centre of town can be seen from both directions

indicators.text: can be seen from both directions
indicators.note: reading the same either way round signals a word that is a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A town's central square visible from either way you approach.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads the same both ways. 'This centre' hints at the phrase civic centre, the main public buildings of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for things belonging to a city or town and its affairs.

clue.text: Greenish, very shimmery in colour

parts.note: iridescent describes colours that shimmer and change with the light

explanation.surface: A shade of green, very shimmering.
explanation.walkthrough: V for 'very' plus IRIDESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending towards green in colour, from the Latin root for green seen in viridian.

clue.text: Prime minister to summon a good round of applause — there's no end to it

parts.note: to call someone is to summon them

indicators.note: no end means the last letter of the applause word is dropped

parts.note: a hand, as in 'give them a big hand', is a round of applause

explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no end to it' cuts D from HAND to leave HAN.
explanation.definitionFit: James Callaghan was Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1976 to 1979.

clue.text: Pressing obsession about injustice not carrying weight

indicators.note: about means the obsession word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to be obsessed with it

indicators.note: not carrying means the weight letter is dropped from the injustice word

parts.note: a wrong is an injustice

explanation.surface: An urgent fixation about unfairness that carries no weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pressing' looks like urgent, but here it means crowding in. 'not carrying weight' drops the W abbreviation from the injustice word.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowds pressing forward or crowding into a place are doing exactly this.

clue.text: Never-ending tax? Home worker gets round it

indicators.note: gets round means the home-and-worker pair is wrapped around the tax

parts.note: in means at home
the worker ant is a crossword staple for 'worker'
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: Complaints about endless taxes, with a home worker trying to get round them.
explanation.walkthrough: Cess is an old word for a local tax; 'it' points back to that tax as the piece that home and worker surround.
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing without pause or interruption is a direct synonym of unceasing.

clue.text: River in the countryside, its source hidden

indicators.note: a river's source is where it begins, so the first letter of the countryside word is concealed

parts.note: rural means of the countryside, here 'in the countryside'

explanation.surface: A river running through farmland, its spring out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: RURAL loses its first letter, its 'source', to leave the answer, a river in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural flows from the Ural Mountains through Russia and Kazakhstan to the Caspian.

clue.text: Going around meadows is perfect joy

indicators.note: going around means the perfect word wraps round the meadows

parts.note: pure means perfect or unblemished
leas are meadows or grassland

explanation.surface: Walking through meadows is complete happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Leas, plural of lea, is a poetic word for meadows that turns up often in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight or enjoyment is a direct synonym for joy.

clue.text: Regretted sounding so curt here?

indicators.note: sounding means the regret word is spoken and heard as another

parts.note: rued means regretted

explanation.surface: Someone regretting how brusque they sounded.
explanation.walkthrough: RUED, spoken, is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite and abrupt in manner; a curt reply is a rude one.

clue.text: Substitute rough material with finer one

parts.note: rep is a ribbed, rather coarse fabric used for upholstery
lace is a fine, delicate material

explanation.surface: Swapping coarse fabric for something more delicate.
explanation.walkthrough: REP, a ribbed upholstery fabric, plus LACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one thing in place of another is a verb sense of substitute.

clue.text: New growth deceived Head of Technology in company at first

indicators.note: at first puts the company piece at the front, before the deceived word
in places the head of technology inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: Coy is the British Army abbreviation for a company

indicators.note: head of means only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: led on means deceived or misled

explanation.surface: A new venture's chief technologist is fooled by the company early on.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes in COY to make COTY, which comes first, then LED ON. COY is the military abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: The first leaf to sprout from a seed is the earliest new growth of a plant.

clue.text: One running pit one about to be sacked

taken as written

clue.text: One refusing to accept old coin

definitions.meaning: someone who says no or denies something
a small French coin of former times

clue.text: Had to be controlled by inner demons?

definitions.meaning: under the sway of an evil spirit

explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of owning, and a word for someone in thrall to demons.

clue.text: Retire, beginning to bleed after protest

clue.text: The way sailor goes across ship brings a smile

definitions.text: The way sailor goes across ship

parts.note: a beam is a broad smile

clue.text: Country girl's taken after mother, backward-looking

backward-looking means the mother word is read from right to left

explanation.walkthrough: 'backward-looking' turns only the mother word, not the girl's name; 'taken after' sets the name behind it.
